column1: description

Our program explores and critically analyzes criminological and sociological explanations of why people commit crimes. It also examines how societies define crime and who is considered a criminal. The Criminology and Justice program approaches the study of crime from an interdisciplinary perspective, drawing on a rich tradition from criminology, sociology, philosophy, psychology and law. In addition to examining why crime is committed, you will be encouraged to think about crime, criminal justice and its administration in ways that are consistent with the principles of fairness, equity, peace and justice.
For more information, please visit the Policing in Society web page.
Celebrating 20+ years!
Modern and forwarding-thinking, Ontario Tech University inspires and equips students and graduates to make a positive impact in a tech-focused world.

Guided by its tech with a conscience ethos, Ontario Tech isn’t only focused on developing the next tech breakthrough. The university is committed to understanding and integrating the social and ethical implications and applications of technology to improve peoples’ lives and the planet.

Each undergraduate student can pursue experiential learning opportunities, allowing them to apply their education and skills to the industry, and strengthen their resumé. The university partners with more than 1,100 organizations across a variety of dynamic sectors—health care, manufacturing, information technology, energy, education, professional and technical services and public administration — to offer hands-on learning opportunities that prepare students for their future careers....

The University of Ottawa is the only bilingual research-intensive university in Canada and the largest bilingual (English-French) university in the world. It welcomes nearly 50,000 students and offers the opportunity to study, work and conduct research in French or English in an environment that is open to Indigenous knowledge and international perspectives.

Located in the heart of Canada’s capital, the University of Ottawa benefits from its immediate proximity to prime democratic institutions, embassies, top research hospitals, national research agencies, a major cultural corridor and a dynamic business environment, all of which support experiential learning, internships and career opportunities....

It is uniquely founded on the principles of flexibility and openness, giving students control over their studies so they can learn whenever and wherever it is right for them.

AU’s open enrolment model helps remove barriers to learning so that anyone 16 years or older can register for most first-year undergraduate courses, regardless of previous education. Campion College offers programs in Arts, Sciences and Media, Art, and Performance, as well as a full complement of pre-professional programs in partnership with the University of Regina. Graduates receive both a University of Regina degree, and a Campion College certificate.

As Canada’s only Jesuit undergraduate college and a federated partner of the University of Regina, Campion offers students the opportunity to pursue their U of R degree as part of the bigger campus while taking advantage of the personalized service and support of a community-within-a-community. It is also part of the International Association of Jesuit Universities (IAJU) which includes over 190 member institutions worldwide.

Any University of Regina student enrolled in the Faculties of Arts; Science; or Media, Art, and Performance can enroll through Campion, including flexible options for those in pre-professional programs. Campion is committed to developing students as a whole to create leaders who truly believe in giving back to their communities by uniting academic excellence with a focus on ethical values and service to others, regardless of their religious affiliation or cultural background. Encouraging students to be agile, courageous and inclusive, the university’s focus on teaching and learning through academic and professional programs is based on a strong liberal arts and science foundation. The people, facilities, programs and services, along with warm prairie hospitality at a compact, cozy campus, combine to set BU apart.
